Source: step 5 of the parent proof, with the flatness estimate (4) at the origin replaced by the hypothesis on spt V cap B_{c_0 rho}(0); the density facts (1a), (1b), (1d) of step 1 of the parent proof are re-derived here from the child monotonicity_bounds. Notation: mu := V.weight, B_t(x) closed balls, omega_n := unitBallVolume n, kappa_m := (p-n)/(4p), Lambda := delta/kappa_m = 4 p delta/(p-n), gamma_b := (1+gamma)/2, theta_0 := (1 - gamma_b)/4 = (1-gamma)/8 in (0, 1/8], C_9 the constant that ConicalApproximationTheorem gives for (n, l) and Lambda~ := 2 omega_n, C_9' := max{C_9, 0}, and C_1 := max{1 + (4e^2 + 2e/omega_n + 1 + 1/omega_n)/kappa_m, (2 omega_n)^(1 - 1/p)} (>= 1). dist(x, T) := infDist x T for the linear subspace T; it is positively homogeneous (dist(tau x, T) = tau dist(x, T) for tau > 0) and 1-Lipschitz. Here 0 < kappa <= theta_0 and 0 < c_0 <= 1/4. Assume 2.3 with 0 < delta <= delta_C, where delta_C is fixed in step 7 depending only on n, l, p, gamma, kappa, c_0; in particular delta <= kappa_m (so Lambda <= 1 and monotonicity_bounds, with (M1) and (M2), applies), delta <= 1/8 and C_1 delta <= 1. All masses below are of balls contained in B_rho(0), hence finite (at most mu(B_rho(0)) <= (1 + delta) omega_n rho^n).

1. Density facts.
 (1a) For 0 < t <= rho: 1 - C_1 delta <= omega_n^-1 t^-n mu(B_t(0)) <= 1 + C_1 delta. Upper bound for t < rho: (M1) with y = 0, R = rho and s = t <= r < rho gives t^-n mu(B_t(0)) <= e^(2 Lambda) r^-n mu(B_r(0)) + 2 e^Lambda Lambda <= e^(2 Lambda) r^-n (1 + delta) omega_n rho^n + 2 e^Lambda Lambda; letting r -> rho, omega_n^-1 t^-n mu(B_t(0)) <= e^(2 Lambda)(1 + delta) + 2 e^Lambda Lambda/omega_n <= (1 + 2e^2 Lambda)(1 + delta) + 2e Lambda/omega_n <= 1 + delta + (4e^2 + 2e/omega_n) Lambda <= 1 + C_1 delta, using e^(2 Lambda) <= 1 + 2 Lambda e^(2 Lambda) <= 1 + 2e^2 Lambda, delta <= 1 and Lambda = delta/kappa_m; for t = rho the upper bound is 2.3 (1 + delta <= 1 + C_1 delta). Lower bound for t < rho: 0 is in spt V (2.3), so (M2) with y = 0, R = rho, s = t gives omega_n^-1 t^-n mu(B_t(0)) >= e^-Lambda (1 - Lambda/omega_n); if 1 - Lambda/omega_n >= 0 this is >= (1 - Lambda)(1 - Lambda/omega_n) >= 1 - Lambda - Lambda/omega_n = 1 - delta (1 + 1/omega_n)/kappa_m >= 1 - C_1 delta, and otherwise 1 - C_1 delta <= 1 - Lambda/omega_n < 0 <= the ratio. For t = rho: mu(B_rho(0)) >= mu(B_t(0)) for every t < rho, so omega_n^-1 rho^-n mu(B_rho(0)) >= (t/rho)^n (1 - C_1 delta) for all t < rho; let t -> rho.
 (1b) For 0 < t <= rho: t^(1-n) integral over B_t(0) of |H| d mu <= C_1 delta. By Hoelder, integral over B_t(0) of |H| <= (integral over B_t(0) of |H|^p)^(1/p) mu(B_t(0))^(1 - 1/p) <= delta rho^(n/p - 1) (2 omega_n t^n)^(1 - 1/p), using rho^(p-n) integral over B_rho(0) of |H|^p <= delta^p (2.3) and mu(B_t(0)) <= (1 + C_1 delta) omega_n t^n <= 2 omega_n t^n ((1a) and C_1 delta <= 1). So t^(1-n) integral over B_t(0) of |H| <= (2 omega_n)^(1-1/p) delta (t/rho)^(1 - n/p) <= C_1 delta. (|H| is mu-integrable on B_t(0), a compact subset of U, because H is locally integrable on U.)
 (1d) For y in spt V cap B_{gamma_b rho}(0) and 0 < s <= (1 - gamma_b) rho/2: mu(B_s(y)) >= omega_n s^n/2. Indeed B_R(y) is contained in B_rho(0) for R := (1 - gamma_b) rho > s, and (M2) gives mu(B_s(y)) >= e^-Lambda (omega_n - Lambda) s^n >= omega_n s^n/2, because Lambda <= min{1/4, omega_n/3} (step 7) gives e^-Lambda >= 3/4 and 1 - Lambda/omega_n >= 2/3.

2. Small |y|. Fix y in spt V cap B_{gamma_b rho}(0). If |y| <= c_0 rho, then y is in spt V cap B_{c_0 rho}(0) and the hypothesis gives dist(y, T) <= (kappa/2)|y| <= kappa |y|.

3. Rescaling for |y| > c_0 rho. Put R := |y|/(1 - theta_0). Since gamma_b + theta_0 = (5 + 3 gamma)/8 < 1, R <= gamma_b rho/(1 - theta_0) < rho, and R > |y| > c_0 rho > 0. By the child rescaled_varifold with c = 0 and scale R there is a contract varifold V~ in U~ := {x : R x in U} (open, as the preimage of U under a continuous map) whose weight mu~ is R^-n times the image of mu under x -> x/R, so that mu~(B_t(x)) = R^-n mu(B_{R t}(R x)) for all x and t, and which has generalized mean curvature H~(x) := R H(R x) in U~ (V has generalized mean curvature H in U by 2.3). B_1(0) is contained in U~ because R B_1(0) = B_R(0) is contained in B_rho(0), which is contained in U. For 0 < t <= 1, the change of variables for the image measure gives integral over B_t(0) of |H~| d mu~ = R R^-n integral over B_{R t}(0) of |H| d mu. Put xi~ := y/R, so |xi~| = 1 - theta_0.
 Hypotheses of 6.1 for V~ with Lambda~ = 2 omega_n, lam := delta, theta := theta_0 and the 6.1-parameter delta~ := 3 C_1 delta: 0 < lam < 1/4 (delta <= 1/8), 0 < theta_0 <= 1/8 < 1/4, and 0 < delta~ < 1/4 (step 7). For every r' in [delta, 1]: |mu~(B_1(0))/omega_n - mu~(B_delta(0))/(omega_n delta^n)| = |omega_n^-1 R^-n mu(B_R(0)) - omega_n^-1 (delta R)^-n mu(B_{delta R}(0))| <= 2 C_1 delta by (1a) (both radii R and delta R lie in (0, rho]), and r'^(1-n) integral over B_{r'}(0) of |H~| d mu~ = (r' R)^(1-n) integral over B_{r' R}(0) of |H| d mu <= C_1 delta by (1b) (0 < r' R <= rho); the sum is <= 3 C_1 delta = delta~. Moreover mu~(B_1(0)) = R^-n mu(B_R(0)) <= (1 + C_1 delta) omega_n <= 2 omega_n = Lambda~.
 Apply the first conclusion of 6.1 with rho~ := kappa/8, which lies in (0, theta_0], and tau := c_0 rho/(2R), which lies in [2 lam, 1] = [2 delta, 1]: tau < 1/2 because R > c_0 rho, and tau > c_0/2 >= 2 delta because R < rho and delta <= c_0/4. Since C_9 delta~^(1/4) |log delta| <= C_9' delta~^(1/4) |log delta|, it gives
 mu~(B_{(1 - delta~^(1/4)) kappa/8}(xi~)) <= tau^-n mu~(B_{tau kappa/8}(tau xi~)) + C_9' delta~^(1/4) |log delta|.

4. Lower bound for the left side. As delta~^(1/4) <= 1/2 (step 7), B_{kappa/16}(xi~) is contained in B_{(1 - delta~^(1/4)) kappa/8}(xi~), so the left side is at least mu~(B_{kappa/16}(xi~)) = R^-n mu(B_{R kappa/16}(y)) >= R^-n omega_n (R kappa/16)^n/2 = omega_n (kappa/16)^n/2 by (1d), since R kappa/16 <= theta_0 rho/16 <= (1 - gamma_b) rho/2.

5. A support point near tau y. As C_9' delta~^(1/4) |log delta| < omega_n (kappa/16)^n/2 (step 7), step 4 forces tau^-n mu~(B_{tau kappa/8}(tau xi~)) > 0, i.e. mu(B_{tau kappa R/8}(tau y)) > 0. Since mu(R^(n+l) minus spt mu) = 0, there is z in spt mu with |z - tau y| <= tau kappa R/8. Then |z| <= tau |y| + tau kappa R/8 = tau R (1 - theta_0 + kappa/8) <= tau R = c_0 rho/2 < rho (kappa/8 <= theta_0). Hence z is in U (B_rho(0) is contained in U), so z is in spt V cap B_{c_0 rho}(0), and by hypothesis dist(z, T) <= (kappa/2)|z| <= (kappa/2)(c_0 rho/2).

6. Conclusion. Using homogeneity, the 1-Lipschitz property and tau^-1 c_0 rho/2 = R: dist(y, T) = tau^-1 dist(tau y, T) <= tau^-1 (dist(z, T) + |z - tau y|) <= tau^-1 ((kappa/2)(c_0 rho/2) + tau kappa R/8) = (kappa/2) R + kappa R/8 = (5/8) kappa R <= (5/8)(8/7) kappa |y| = (5/7) kappa |y| <= kappa |y|, because R = |y|/(1 - theta_0) <= (8/7)|y| (theta_0 <= 1/8). Together with step 2 this proves dist(y, T) <= kappa |y| for every y in spt V cap B_{(1+gamma) rho/2}(0).

7. Choice of delta_C. delta_C > 0 is the minimum of: kappa_m; kappa_m min{1/4, omega_n/3} (so Lambda <= min{1/4, omega_n/3}, used in (1d)); 1/C_1 (so C_1 delta <= 1); 1/8 (so delta < 1/4); 1/(48 C_1) (so 3 C_1 delta <= 1/16 < 1/4 and delta~^(1/4) <= 1/2); c_0/4; and a number delta_5 in (0, 1) such that C_9' (3 C_1 delta)^(1/4) |log delta| < omega_n (kappa/16)^n/2 for all delta in (0, delta_5], which exists because delta^(1/4) |log delta| -> 0 as delta -> 0+ (Mathlib tendsto_log_mul_rpow_nhdsGT_zero). These depend only on n, l, p, gamma, kappa, c_0 (C_9 = C_9(n, l, 2 omega_n)), so delta_C is chosen before U, V, H, delta, rho and T, as the order of quantifiers requires.
